jobs.title: Director, Delivery CX AI
jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

Compensation Range: CA$150K - CA$190K

jobs.title: Canada Transformation Office Leader
jobs.description:
We are seeking a talented individual to join our Transformation team at Marsh Risk. This role will be based in Toronto. This is a hybrid role that has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office.

As the Canada Transformation Office Leader, you will help shape and deliver the region’s most important strategic priorities. This is a highly visible leadership role that will work closely with Canada’s senior executive team, focused on turning strategy into execution—driving outcomes, enabling change, and building momentum across the business.

This is an opportunity to lead the Transformation Office team in Canada, oversee delivery of high-impact initiatives, serve as a key connector between Canada leadership and broader enterprise transformation efforts and shape how Canada executes strategy—building the operating rhythm, governance, and storytelling that drives results.

We will count on you to:

You will be accountable for translating strategic priorities into measurable results, with responsibilities including:

Lead and develop the Canada Transformation Office team, setting clear direction, priorities, and a high-performance culture
Drive execution of high-profile, cross-functional initiatives from concept through delivery—ensuring scope, timelines, risks, and dependencies are actively managed
Partner with Canada business leaders to define transformation roadmaps and solve complex, ambiguous problems with practical, actionable plans
Align Canada initiatives with broader cross-regional strategy, ensuring consistency while tailoring approaches to local business needs
Create executive-ready narratives and materials (e.g., updates, business cases, progress reporting, and stakeholder communications) that clearly “tell the story” and accelerate decision-making
Represent the Transformation Office for Canada, acting as a trusted advisor and point of connection across stakeholders and teams

What you need to have: 

10+ years of experience in strategy, operations, finance, banking, project/program management, consulting, or a related role
4+ years of people leadership experience, with a track record of building, coaching, and motivating teams
Demonstrated experience supporting or leading organizational change, transformation, or large-scale initiatives (does not need to be a dedicated transformation role)
Bachelor’s degree required; MBA preferred
Strong executive presence with excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to and influencing senior leaders
A self-starter mindset with urgency, curiosity, and sound judgment—able to navigate ambiguity, connect dots quickly, and propose solutions
Proven ability to work across functions, manage competing priorities, and drive progress through stakeholders without direct authority

Why join our team:

We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being.

Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Marsh is committed to embracing a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005, Marsh will provide a reasonable accommodation to employees and prospective employees to the point of undue hardship upon request and as required in respect of the individual’s particular restrictions and limitations. If you require a specific accommodation because of a disability or medical need, please contact reasonableaccommodations@marsh.com.

Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

This is a New position.

jobs.title: Leader, Software Product Development Process Transformation – Connected Vehicles
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Connected Vehicle Engineering Director, the Leader, Software Product Development Process Transformation is responsible for evolving the practices, processes, methods, and tools supporting the design, development, integration, and validation of connected vehicle solutions.

In an environment where software is a strategic component of BRP products, you will contribute to the continuous improvement of software engineering practices while ensuring their seamless integration into the overall product development lifecycle. Working closely with software, systems, architecture, integration, validation, and project management teams, you will help enhance product quality, delivery predictability, and organizational efficiency.

You’ll Have The Opportunity To

Define and roll out new software product development processes tailored to a centralized group delivering software solutions across all product lines.
Align working methods across software, systems, architecture, integration, and validation teams.
Drive the implementation of software engineering best practices, requirements management, integration, and validation.
Promote the adoption of methodologies and tools that improve quality, efficiency, and cross-team collaboration.
Establish the transformation roadmap and lead its execution within the Connected Vehicle group, ensuring consistency and compatibility with product line engineering teams' practices.
Develop and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the maturity, efficiency, and quality of development processes.
Train, coach, and support teams and managers through change management and the adoption of new practices.
Support initiatives related to automation, software quality, and continuous improvement.

YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE THE FOLLOWING SKILLS AND QUALITIES:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field; 12+ years of relevant experience in software development, including significant experience in process definition or transformation.
A strong understanding of the product development lifecycle and cross-disciplinary engineering interactions.
Proven experience in process improvement, organizational transformation, or operational excellence.
Knowledge of modern software development, quality assurance, and continuous integration practices.
Strong leadership, communication, and influencing skills to align multidisciplinary teams around a shared vision.
Clear accountability for delivery and drive to achieve transformation objectives.

Assets That Will Set You Apart

Experience with Atlassian tools (Jira, Confluence) and DevOps platforms (CI/CD pipelines).
Experience in connected vehicles, embedded systems, or the automotive/powersports industry.
Experience managing multi-product projects within an engineering environment.

Do you have other skills? Tell us what makes you unique and why you would be a great addition to the team.

ACKNOWLEDGING THE POWER OF DIVERSITY

BRP is dedicated to nurturing a culture that invites, connects, and propels the ambitions of people of all backgrounds, profiles, beliefs and experiences. Ultimately, the diversity and uniqueness of our people fuel our ingenuity and set the course for the path ahead!

For this reason, we value diversity and we strive to always push each other forward to build an inclusive workplace where every employee feels like they belong, where they can grow and find meaning.

AT BRP, WHEN WE TALK ABOUT BENEFITS, WE GO ALL IN.

Let’s start with a strong foundation — You want it, we have it:

Annual bonus based on the company’s financial results
Generous paid time away
Pension plan
Collective saving opportunities
Industry leading healthcare fully paid by BRP

What About Some Feel Good Perks

Flexible work schedule
A summer schedule that varies by department and location
Holiday season shutdown
Educational resources
Discount on BRP products

WELCOME TO BRP

We’re a world leader in recreational vehicles and boats, creating innovative ways to move on snow, water, asphalt, dirt and even in the air. Headquartered in the Canadian town of Valcourt, Quebec, our company is rooted in a spirit of ingenuity and intense customer focus. Today, we operate manufacturing facilities in Canada, the United States, Mexico, Finland, Australia and Austria, with a workforce made up of close to 17,000 spirited people, all driven by the deeply held belief that at work, as with life itself, it’s not about the destination: It’s about the journey.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Director of Finance provides strategic leadership and overall direction for the finance department at Lopes Limited. As a key partner to the President, Vice-President and senior leadership team, the Director translates business priorities into financial plans, provides clear advice on financial performance and risk, and supports decisions that strengthen profitability, cash flow and long-term growth.
Reporting to the President, the Director is accountable for the quality, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting and for the effectiveness of accounting operations, financial controls and forecasting. The role leads and develops the finance team, establishes clear accountabilities and ensures financial information supports practical decisions across construction, fabrication and project operations.
The primary focus is Lopes Limited. When requested by ownership or senior leadership, the Director also provides financial guidance to sister companies, working with their management teams and finance personnel to strengthen planning, reporting and financial practices within the scope assigned.

What we offer as an employer

Competitive salary
Comprehensive benefits including dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
Company RRSP’s
Wellness and employee assistance programs
Opportunities to grow within your community
Company events
Work-life balance
Free Golf Membership
On-site medical clinic
On-site service center for vehicle repairs at discounted rates
A culture that is built on respect, health, safety, and integrity

Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership:
Lead Lopes Limited’s financial strategy, advise senior leadership, evaluate investments and growth opportunities, and guide commercial decisions to strengthen profitability and financial resilience.
Forecasting and Performance:
Lead forecasting and financial reporting, while coaching department leaders to manage spend, understand results, and take corrective action
Financial Reporting and Project Profitability:
Manage financial closing, reporting, project & departmental costing, and external accountant coordination to ensure accurate financial statements, reliable performance analysis, and sound accounting practices.
Cash Flow Financing and Capital Planning:
Oversee cash flow, working capital, financing, banking relationships, including financial oversight of bonding, insurance and funding opportunities.
Financial Controls Compliance and Risk:
Direct financial policies, internal controls, risk management, tax compliance, secure records and intercompany accounting to ensure accurate reporting and financial accountability.
Finance Department Leadership:
Lead and develop the finance team, oversee accounting and payroll, support workforce and compensation planning, and improve financial systems, processes and coordination across departments.

Qualifications and Experience

Post-secondary education in accounting or business with a CPA designation or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Eight to ten years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership of a finance team and responsibility for financial planning, reporting, and controls
Experience in construction, fabrication, industrial services, or other project-based business, with a strong understanding of job costing, work in progress, and revenue recognition.
Demonstrated ability to advise senior leadership, develop financial strategy, and translate complex information into clear recommendations.
Strong experience in forecasting and cash flow management.
Knowledge of Canadian accounting and tax requirements, with the judgement to engage specialized advisors when needed.
Experience managing relationships with external accountants, and other financial partners; exposure to multiple related companies is an asset.
Advanced Excel and financial systems skills, including the ability to improve reporting and use data to support decisions.
Proven people leadership, sound business judgement, and the ability to challenge assumptions respectfully while building productive working relationships.
High standards of integrity, accuracy, and confidentiality, with the ability to balance strategic priorities and operational deadlines.

We thank all candidates for their interest but only those considered for an interview will be contacted.

At Lopes Limited we are committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We offer a barrier free experience to applicants with accessibility needs. Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage during the recruitment process. Please contact us directly for such arrangements at jobs@lopes.ca

Salary Range: $90,000 - $150,000

jobs.title: Senior Director, IAM Product, Architecture, and Governance
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 274541

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Senior Director IAM Product, Architecture and Governance will lead both the Product Management, Architecture, and Application Governance functions for the Scotiabank’s global IAM services, supporting both external customers and enterprise workforce platforms, working to accelerate new product enhancements in alignment with business partners, fraud, and technology teams.

The incumbent will provide overall strategic product roadmaps, architectural design of IAM platforms, and ongoing governance models for supported applications which leverage IAM services, ensuring compliance with Scotiabank’s Technology Policy and Standards, global regulations, and industry standard security practices.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Oversee Product Management for IAM Services and Platforms

Establish and lead Product Management for Customer IAM and Workforce IAM, defining intake, prioritization, requirements, and architectural alignment, while managing a team of Product Managers responsible for backlogs, features, and enhancements across customer and enterprise IAM domains.
Own the IAM product strategy and roadmap for enterprise and consumer platforms, partnering with business channels, fraud technology, Engineering, and key stakeholders to align critical capabilities, oversee execution (including vendor selection, MVP definition, rollout planning), and adapt priorities as conditions change.
Drive outcomes, funding, and continuous improvement, developing business cases and funding models in partnership with Technology, PMO, and Finance, establishing stakeholder feedback loops and KPIs for adoption, and maintaining strong awareness of industry trends, emerging IAM capabilities, and fraud protection advancements.

Responsible for Enterprise Grade IAM Services and Platforms

Lead and govern IAM architecture delivery, overseeing a team of domain architects responsible for designing scalable, resilient solutions that meet business requirements, adhere to security by design principles, and align with Enterprise Architecture standards and technology direction.
Drive cross bank architectural collaboration, partnering with Product Management, Engineering, security architecture, fraud, compliance, and business channel teams to design new platforms and features, align on integration patterns, and deliver secure, end to end IAM solutions.
Own architectural assessment and IAM technical leadership, defining the intake and assessment process for new features and enhancements (including cost and timeline estimates), guiding engineering execution, and representing IAM as the technology SME on enterprise wide transformation initiatives.

IAM Application Governance

Establish and lead the IAM Governance and Control function, ensuring global application compliance with Scotiabank Technology Policies and Standards, regional regulatory requirements, and external audit expectations across customer and workforce platforms.
Define and operate sustainable governance processes and tooling, including application inventory, compliance tracking, and control effectiveness measurement, with clear KPIs that track adoption and maturity of IAM key controls enterprise wide.
Provide strategic IAM governance leadership and SME support, partnering with Product, Architecture, regional CISOs, and all lines of defense to align KPIs and methodologies, guide remediation of control gaps, and evolve governance as IAM platforms modernize.

General Accountabilities

Understand how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.
Create an environment in which their team pursues effective and efficient operations of their respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.
Build a high performance environment and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviors; communicating vison/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.
Lead and drive a customer focused, practical, and secure, culture throughout their team to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems, and knowledge.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Minimum of a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) required
7+ years’ experience in a Product Management (or equivalent) capacity required
7+ years in an IAM Architect Role.
8+ years’ experience in Information Security or Information Technology
10+ years working with IAM platforms
Previous exposure to Regulatory, Compliance, Risk and Audit functions
Experience developing and documenting IAM directives, standards and policies.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Strong planning and organizational skills; can manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
Experience in the information security industry and with security software products
Excellent understanding on financial principles of large enterprise organization
Experience in working with complex processes
Willing to learn and grow, and demonstrates resilience to ever-changing priorities

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons, contests, Humans of Digital and much more

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

jobs.description:
We invite you to Explore the Potential of being part of something Clearly Essential!

Compass Minerals (NYSE: CMP) is a leading global provider of essential minerals focused on safely delivering where and when it matters to help solve nature’s challenges for customers and communities. The company’s salt products help keep roadways safe during winter weather and are used in numerous other consumer, industrial, chemical and agricultural applications. Its plant nutrition products help improve the quality and yield of crops while supporting sustainable agriculture. Compass Minerals operates 11 production and packaging facilities with more than 1,800 employees throughout the U.S., Canada and the U.K. Visit compassminerals.com for more information about the company and its products.

We are seeking a Director, FP&A - Site Operations
to join our team in Goderich, Ontario
. The Director, FP&A - Site Operations serves as the finance leader for the Goderich Mine and acts as an extension of Corporate Finance and FP&A. This role is responsible for leading all site finance activities, including financial planning and analysis, accounting review, financial reporting, internal controls support, budgeting and forecasting. As a key member of the site leadership team, this position partners closely with business operations leaders to optimize financial and cost performance, support operational excellence, productivity initiatives and evaluate capital investment decisions. This role is accountable for ensuring financial integrity, compliance and the delivery of actionable insights that support achievement of business objectives.

Why Join Compass Minerals?

Competitive Pay & Benefits – Medical, dental, vision, disability coverage, EAP, tuition reimbursement, and more.
Work-Life Balance – Paid vacation, sick time, and floating holidays.
Retirement Support – Defined Contribution Pension Plan with company contributions.
Values-Driven Culture – Built on Integrity, Respect, Collaboration, Value Creation, and High Performance.
Safety First – Committed to a safe, inclusive workplace and our Zero Harm goal.
Meaningful Work – Make an impact through work that helps keep people safe, feed the world, and enrich lives.
Career Growth – Ongoing learning and development opportunities to support your success.

Key Responsibilities

FP&A Business Partnership

Partner with operations leadership and Corporate Finance & Accounting to align financial and business priorities.
Drive performance through financial insights, strategic guidance and data-driven decision-making.
Lead financial reviews, identify and communicate trends, risks and opportunities and provide actionable recommendations to leadership.
Present forecasts, financial results and variance analyses, providing clear insights to support business decisions.
Lead the site’s annual budgeting, recurring forecasting and long-range planning processes.
Develop financial models, scenario analyses and performance reporting to evaluate the financial impact of operational initiatives.
Establish and analyze performance metrics that drive profitability and achievement of strategic objectives.
Partner with Finance to analyze and communicate monthly financial performance against the plan, forecast, and prior-year results.
Drive forecast accuracy and strategic planning through trend analysis, market research and future performance scenarios.
Provide financial leadership for capital investments, productivity initiatives and operational improvement projects through business case development, ROI analysis and post-investment reviews.
Champion a culture of continuous improvement by utilizing operational and financial performance metrics to identify process enhancement opportunities and drive sustainable results.

Manufacturing Finance & Accounting

Analyze manufacturing performance and cost drivers, providing insights to operations leadership.
Provide oversight of standard costing, inventory valuation and related financial records to ensure results accurately reflect operating performance.
Support internal and external audits and ensure compliance with accounting policies and reporting requirements.
Support the Manager of Accounting in monitoring internal controls and financial processes to manage risk and ensure compliance.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach and develop site finance personnel through talent development, succession planning and performance management.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement and business partnership.
Promote consistent processes, reporting and best practices across the finance and accounting organization.
Perform other related duties as required.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
10+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience in a manufacturing environment.
Experience as a Controller, Plant Controller, Site Controller or similar manufacturing finance leadership role.
Strong expertise in FP&A, manufacturing accounting, cost accounting, inventory accounting and internal controls.
Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with operations leadership and influence business decisions.
Experience leading, developing and mentoring accounting and finance teams.
Strong ERP, financial systems, analytical and communication skills.

new_jobs.title: Director, Delivery CX AI
new_jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

Compensation Range: CA$150K - CA$190K

new_jobs.title: Leader, Software Product Development Process Transformation – Connected Vehicles
new_jobs.description:
Reporting to the Connected Vehicle Engineering Director, the Leader, Software Product Development Process Transformation is responsible for evolving the practices, processes, methods, and tools supporting the design, development, integration, and validation of connected vehicle solutions.

In an environment where software is a strategic component of BRP products, you will contribute to the continuous improvement of software engineering practices while ensuring their seamless integration into the overall product development lifecycle. Working closely with software, systems, architecture, integration, validation, and project management teams, you will help enhance product quality, delivery predictability, and organizational efficiency.

You’ll Have The Opportunity To

Define and roll out new software product development processes tailored to a centralized group delivering software solutions across all product lines.
Align working methods across software, systems, architecture, integration, and validation teams.
Drive the implementation of software engineering best practices, requirements management, integration, and validation.
Promote the adoption of methodologies and tools that improve quality, efficiency, and cross-team collaboration.
Establish the transformation roadmap and lead its execution within the Connected Vehicle group, ensuring consistency and compatibility with product line engineering teams' practices.
Develop and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the maturity, efficiency, and quality of development processes.
Train, coach, and support teams and managers through change management and the adoption of new practices.
Support initiatives related to automation, software quality, and continuous improvement.

YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE THE FOLLOWING SKILLS AND QUALITIES:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field; 12+ years of relevant experience in software development, including significant experience in process definition or transformation.
A strong understanding of the product development lifecycle and cross-disciplinary engineering interactions.
Proven experience in process improvement, organizational transformation, or operational excellence.
Knowledge of modern software development, quality assurance, and continuous integration practices.
Strong leadership, communication, and influencing skills to align multidisciplinary teams around a shared vision.
Clear accountability for delivery and drive to achieve transformation objectives.

Assets That Will Set You Apart

Experience with Atlassian tools (Jira, Confluence) and DevOps platforms (CI/CD pipelines).
Experience in connected vehicles, embedded systems, or the automotive/powersports industry.
Experience managing multi-product projects within an engineering environment.

Do you have other skills? Tell us what makes you unique and why you would be a great addition to the team.

ACKNOWLEDGING THE POWER OF DIVERSITY

BRP is dedicated to nurturing a culture that invites, connects, and propels the ambitions of people of all backgrounds, profiles, beliefs and experiences. Ultimately, the diversity and uniqueness of our people fuel our ingenuity and set the course for the path ahead!

For this reason, we value diversity and we strive to always push each other forward to build an inclusive workplace where every employee feels like they belong, where they can grow and find meaning.

AT BRP, WHEN WE TALK ABOUT BENEFITS, WE GO ALL IN.

Let’s start with a strong foundation — You want it, we have it:

Annual bonus based on the company’s financial results
Generous paid time away
Pension plan
Collective saving opportunities
Industry leading healthcare fully paid by BRP

What About Some Feel Good Perks

Flexible work schedule
A summer schedule that varies by department and location
Holiday season shutdown
Educational resources
Discount on BRP products

WELCOME TO BRP

We’re a world leader in recreational vehicles and boats, creating innovative ways to move on snow, water, asphalt, dirt and even in the air. Headquartered in the Canadian town of Valcourt, Quebec, our company is rooted in a spirit of ingenuity and intense customer focus. new_jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 274541

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Senior Director IAM Product, Architecture and Governance will lead both the Product Management, Architecture, and Application Governance functions for the Scotiabank’s global IAM services, supporting both external customers and enterprise workforce platforms, working to accelerate new product enhancements in alignment with business partners, fraud, and technology teams.

The incumbent will provide overall strategic product roadmaps, architectural design of IAM platforms, and ongoing governance models for supported applications which leverage IAM services, ensuring compliance with Scotiabank’s Technology Policy and Standards, global regulations, and industry standard security practices.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Oversee Product Management for IAM Services and Platforms

Establish and lead Product Management for Customer IAM and Workforce IAM, defining intake, prioritization, requirements, and architectural alignment, while managing a team of Product Managers responsible for backlogs, features, and enhancements across customer and enterprise IAM domains.
Own the IAM product strategy and roadmap for enterprise and consumer platforms, partnering with business channels, fraud technology, Engineering, and key stakeholders to align critical capabilities, oversee execution (including vendor selection, MVP definition, rollout planning), and adapt priorities as conditions change.
Drive outcomes, funding, and continuous improvement, developing business cases and funding models in partnership with Technology, PMO, and Finance, establishing stakeholder feedback loops and KPIs for adoption, and maintaining strong awareness of industry trends, emerging IAM capabilities, and fraud protection advancements.

Responsible for Enterprise Grade IAM Services and Platforms

Lead and govern IAM architecture delivery, overseeing a team of domain architects responsible for designing scalable, resilient solutions that meet business requirements, adhere to security by design principles, and align with Enterprise Architecture standards and technology direction.
Drive cross bank architectural collaboration, partnering with Product Management, Engineering, security architecture, fraud, compliance, and business channel teams to design new platforms and features, align on integration patterns, and deliver secure, end to end IAM solutions.
Own architectural assessment and IAM technical leadership, defining the intake and assessment process for new features and enhancements (including cost and timeline estimates), guiding engineering execution, and representing IAM as the technology SME on enterprise wide transformation initiatives.

IAM Application Governance

Establish and lead the IAM Governance and Control function, ensuring global application compliance with Scotiabank Technology Policies and Standards, regional regulatory requirements, and external audit expectations across customer and workforce platforms.
Define and operate sustainable governance processes and tooling, including application inventory, compliance tracking, and control effectiveness measurement, with clear KPIs that track adoption and maturity of IAM key controls enterprise wide.
Provide strategic IAM governance leadership and SME support, partnering with Product, Architecture, regional CISOs, and all lines of defense to align KPIs and methodologies, guide remediation of control gaps, and evolve governance as IAM platforms modernize.

General Accountabilities

Understand how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.
Create an environment in which their team pursues effective and efficient operations of their respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.
Build a high performance environment and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviors; communicating vison/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.
Lead and drive a customer focused, practical, and secure, culture throughout their team to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems, and knowledge.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Minimum of a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) required
7+ years’ experience in a Product Management (or equivalent) capacity required
7+ years in an IAM Architect Role.
8+ years’ experience in Information Security or Information Technology
10+ years working with IAM platforms
Previous exposure to Regulatory, Compliance, Risk and Audit functions
Experience developing and documenting IAM directives, standards and policies.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Strong planning and organizational skills; can manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
Experience in the information security industry and with security software products
Excellent understanding on financial principles of large enterprise organization
Experience in working with complex processes
Willing to learn and grow, and demonstrates resilience to ever-changing priorities

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.

Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons, contests, Humans of Digital and much more
